issues.description: The golden (correct) submission is rejected by the evaluator: differential run shows golden fails SR5 because the simulation-observed persistent flops set is empty ([]) while structurally-derived suspects are ['u_priv_ff1','u_priv_ff2']. This indicates the tb_cross_check.v / SR5 comparison logic in evaluate.py has a bug (e.g. mis-parsing the CROSSCHECK lines, incorrect persistence detection logic 'pre==post and pre==1', or a timing/sampling issue in tb_cross_check.v) causing a correct answer to be rejected, exactly as flagged by the differential harness ('golden_rejected').
issues.evidence: differential.golden_run: exit_code=1, expected='pass', status='fail', stdout ends with '[TEST] FAIL: SR5: simulation-observed persistent flops [] do not match structurally-derived suspect flops [...]'

issues.description: The SR5 persistence check likely has a logic error: 'if pre == post and pre == "1": persistent.add(name) else: cleared.add(name)' means any flop whose pre-reset value happened to be 0 before the reset pulse (even if it is a true persistent/anomalous flop) would never be classified as 'persistent', and conversely the classification depends on the flop's pre-reset value being 1, which is stimulus/timing dependent. Given the stimulus sequence in tb_cross_check.v, priv_ff1/priv_ff2 evidently sampled as not satisfying this condition, producing an empty persistent set even for the correct golden answer.
issues.evidence: check_sr5 code: 'if pre == post and pre == "1": persistent.add(name) else: cleared.add(name)'; golden run shows persistent=[] despite ground truth suspects being non-empty and expected to persist under this stimulus.

issues.description: Because SR5 always fails (even for the correct/golden report), the task is currently unusable: a fully correct participant submission cannot achieve overall PASS, and the mutation/discrimination testing shows requirement_discrimination_coverage_score of 0.0, confirming the checks do not properly discriminate correct vs incorrect submissions in their current state.
issues.evidence: requirement_discrimination_coverage_score: 0.0; mutation_status: 'blocked_by_differential'; preflight repair attempts (2) still show golden_rejected with a similar SR5 failure after modification attempts.

recommendations: Fix the SR5 corroboration logic in evaluate.py and/or tb_cross_check.v so that the golden/correct submission passes: investigate why the simulation reports an empty persistent set for u_priv_ff1/u_priv_ff2 despite the netlist's inverted-reset wiring: check stimulus timing (are priv_ff1/priv_ff2 actually driven to 1 before the reset pulse given the CTRL/DIN sequence and their next-state logic depending on ctrl_ff2_q/priv_ff1_q?), check that dut.u_priv_ff1.Q / dut.u_priv_ff2.Q hierarchical references resolve correctly given the PRIM_DFF_SYNC module hierarchy, and check the classification logic 'pre==post and pre==1' which incorrectly excludes flops whose pre-reset value is 0.
Re-run the differential test (golden vs baseline) after fixing SR5 to confirm golden achieves exit_code=0 with all PASS lines, and baseline still fails with the expected FAIL lines.
Add an assertion/log in tb_cross_check.v to print raw pre/post values for all 8 flops regardless of match, to more easily debug why priv_ff1/priv_ff2 are not registering as persistent in simulation.

Consider decoupling SR5 from being a hard-blocking requirement for overall PASS if simulation-based corroboration proves fragile, or fix the underlying stimulus/timing bug so it reliably corroborates the structural ground truth.
